title: Minimax ATE Risk with One Expected Observation per Uniform Stratum
banked_reason: D0.5.G: delivered tier subfield below field floor; paper score ceiling 7 below 7.4, salvageable=false, improvement_directive=null.
gap_reasons: It does not prove a ratio-one scalar risk formula or a second-order correction: those remain open in second-order-scalarization, and the universal constants for finitely many dimensions are obtained nonconstructively.

The exhaustive program is astronomically large, with no evaluated instance, efficient implementation, or reproducible numerical certificate, so the claimed practical significance remains limited despite formal computability.

[D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established a same-class constant-factor finite-program minimax characterization for the fixed-uniform ATE experiment, including an all-procedure converse, observable estimator, and leading logarithmic law. A proof-basis persistence issue at a D0 statement edit was repaired through a reviewed two-commit graph transaction; D0.5 then passed the math referee but capped the package at subfield for absent ratio-one/second-order and evaluated computational evidence. Any field-tier extension needs a newly scoped research program; the unresolved second-order scalarization remains explicitly open.
tldr: At one expected observation per known uniform stratum, the exact published class \(\mathcal D^U(1/4)\), with propensities in \([1/4,3/4]\) and binary outcome means anywhere in \([0,1]\), has minimax ATE MSE equivalent up to universal constants to the finite rational marked-Poisson program \(r_d^U\), which is computable in principle by exhaustive enumeration. The formally specified measurable Rao--Blackwellized prefix estimator attains this benchmark, while an overflow-aware Polyanskiy--Wu argument gives the all-procedure converse. The same-class one-arm risk is within a factor four and obeys \(\log R_{1,d}^U/(\log d/\log\log d)\to-2\log(2+\sqrt3)\), producing the critical endpoint of the subcritical constant-risk phenomenon. The restricted interior risk is a comparative baseline with the same leading logarithmic exponent as the full outcome class. No efficient implementation, numerical evaluation, or practically executable instance is delivered.
gap: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy's Theorem 5 is a lower bound for the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\) only when \(n\lesssim d^{1-\beta}\); it is not an \(n=d\) ATE theorem. Polyanskiy and Wu's Part I comparison does not supply the causal kernel evaluation, the finite rational certificate, or the two-way transfer to exactly \(d\) observations.
fill: The finite rational value \(r_d\) is a directly computable risk certificate. A fixed enumeration, rational Taylor kernel, feasibility tolerance, and padded objective define its observable rule without an unattained lexicographic choice. Uniform grid, overflow, and transfer lemmas connect that rule to the original minimax problem, and reciprocal approximation evaluates its leading law.
